findings.title: plot() crashes with cryptic 'cannot unpack non-iterable NoneType' whenever >3-D data reaches the drawing layer (reduce instance with n_components>3; reduce=None)
findings.description: plot()'s second internal reduce call (plot.py lines 1752-1757) trusts reduce() to bring data to <=3 dims, but two documented-adjacent specs defeat it: (a) reduce=PCA(n_components=5) -- the docstring says reduce accepts an 'instance', and reduce() honors an already-configured instance's n_components over ndims (warning 'Unequal values passed to dims and n_components. Using the already-configured model instance.', emitted twice) and returns 5-D data; (b) reduce=None (the 'skip this stage' idiom every other stage kwarg accepts) makes reduce() a no-op, leaving e.g. 10-D data. Either way matplotlib_backend.dispatch_static() has no >3-D branch and returns None, so the caller's tuple-unpack raises TypeError with no mention of dimensionality, reduce, or ndims. The equivalent string spec (reduce='PCA', ndims=10) works fine (plots 3-D).

import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
x = np.random.default_rng(3).normal(0, 1, (50, 10))
hyp.plot(x, fmt='.', reduce=PCA(n_components=5), show=False)  # TypeError
# also: hyp.plot(x, fmt='.', reduce=None, show=False)  # same TypeError
findings.expected: Either plot in 3-D like reduce='PCA', ndims=5 does (reduce the 5-D result to 3 for display, returning the 5-D data via return_model), or raise a clear ValueError naming the >3-D data and suggesting ndims=/a <=3-component instance.

findings.title: reduce=<fitted Reducer> is documented for plot() but always crashes: plot re-applies the fitted model to its own already-reduced 3-column output
findings.description: plot()'s docstring types reduce as 'str, dict, class, instance, or fitted Reducer'. hyp.reduce(new_data, reduce=fitted) alone works (returns (30, 3)). But plot() reduces twice: analyze() applies the fitted 10-feature->3 model correctly, then the second call reducer(xform, ndims=3, reduce=reduce, ...) (plot.py line 1756) passes the SAME fitted model the now-3-column data, and sklearn rejects the feature-count mismatch. Every plot(reduce=<fitted Reducer>) call on data wider than 3 columns therefore fails, so the documented fit-once/re-plot workflow via a fitted Reducer is unusable (the pipeline=/return_model bundle path does work).

hyp.plot(rng.normal(0, 1, (30, 10)), fmt='.', reduce=model, show=False)  # ValueError

findings.title: align=False raises ValueError('unknown model: False') though plot()/align()/analyze() docstrings all promise 'If False or None, no alignment is applied'
findings.description: hypertools/tools/align.py line 74 only short-circuits `if align is None:`; False falls through to the dispatcher and dies in hypertools/core/shared.py ('unknown model: False'). All three public entry points crash identically: hyp.plot(data, align=False), hyp.align(data, align=False), hyp.analyze(data, align=False). normalize=False works correctly, making the stage kwargs inconsistent with each other as well as with their shared docstring wording.
findings.expected: No alignment applied (identical to align=None), per the docstring of plot(), align(), and analyze().
findings.actual: ValueError: unknown model: False  (raised from hypertools/core/shared.py:143/154 via hypertools/tools/align.py, which only handles `align is None`)

findings.title: cluster=False raises ValueError('Invalid cluster model specified') though plot()'s docstring types cluster as 'str, dict, False, or None'
findings.description: plot.py line 1867 gates the cluster branch on `cluster is not None`, so False enters the branch, matches neither the str nor the dict arm, and hits the line-1905 ValueError. The docstring (line 594) explicitly lists False as an accepted 'off' value, and the sibling kwargs normalize=False (works) and align=False (finding -003) share the same documented convention. The error message also fails to mention that None/False is how you disable clustering.
findings.expected: No clustering (identical to cluster=None), per the documented type 'str, dict, False, or None'.
findings.actual: ValueError: Invalid cluster model specified; should be string or dictionary!

findings.title: Misspelled pipeline kwargs (n_dims, nclusters, allign, normalise) run the whole pipeline then surface as a matplotlib artist AttributeError (or a plotly 'ignoring' warning + silently-default plot)
findings.description: Because of the GH #206 **kwargs passthrough, a typo'd stage kwarg is treated as an artist style property. matplotlib backend: the full pipeline runs, then drawing fails with `AttributeError: Line2D.set() got an unexpected keyword argument 'n_dims'` -- the user is pointed at matplotlib line properties, not at plot()'s own `ndims` parameter, and gets no did-you-mean. plotly backend is worse in effect: `UserWarning: backend='plotly' cannot map the following extra kwarg(s) to a trace property and will ignore them: ['n_dims'].` and then renders a DEFAULT-pipeline figure -- a scientist who intended ndims=2 gets a 3-D default plot that 'worked'. Suggest fuzzy-matching extra kwargs against plot()'s named parameters and raising/warning with a did-you-mean.
findings.expected: An error (or at least a warning) suggesting the correct parameter, e.g. "unexpected keyword 'n_dims' -- did you mean 'ndims'?", before the pipeline runs.
findings.actual: AttributeError: Line2D.set() got an unexpected keyword argument 'n_dims'  |  plotly: UserWarning: backend='plotly' cannot map the following extra kwarg(s) to a trace property and will ignore them: ['n_dims']. (figure renders with default ndims=3 pipeline)

findings.title: Invalid normalize= value raises a self-contradictory AssertionError that names the internal 'scale_type' and lists 'none' as accepted -- but normalize='none' raises the same assertion
findings.description: hyp.plot(data, normalize='columns') (and normalize=True, and normalize='none') all raise `AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.` from hypertools/tools/normalize.py line 242. Three problems: (1) AssertionError instead of ValueError (stripped under python -O; inconsistent with reduce/align/cluster which raise ValueError); (2) 'scale_type' is an internal name -- the user-facing kwarg is `normalize`; (3) the message lists 'none' among accepted values, yet passing the string 'none' trips the very same assertion (only the Python literals False/None work).
findings.expected: ValueError naming the `normalize` kwarg and its actually-accepted values ('across', 'within', 'row', False, None); the string 'none' should either work or not be advertised.
findings.actual: AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.

findings.title: Integer-valued group labels passed as hue= are silently treated as CONTINUOUS values (no grouping, no legend possible); only non-numeric labels group categorically -- the docstring never states this dtype rule
findings.description: hue=np.repeat(['a','b','c'],30) yields 3 grouped traces and a working legend; hue=np.repeat([0,1,2],30) (or the same as a Python int list) yields a continuous-colormap rendering (n_lines=0, per-point colors) and legend=True is rejected with 'legend is not supported for continuous or matrix-valued hue; ignoring legend.' Scientists' group IDs are very often ints; the docstring ('Accepts categorical labels (one per observation; grouped and colored by category), continuous numeric values (mapped through the palette)...') gives no way to know ints land on the continuous path or how to force categorical treatment (casting to str is the workaround).
findings.repro:
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '/Users/jmanning/hypertools')
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
rng = np.random.default_rng(5)
D = np.vstack([rng.normal(i * 6, 1, (30, 8)) for i in range(3)])
fig = hyp.plot(D, fmt='.', hue=np.repeat([0, 1, 2], 30), legend=True, show=False)
print(len(fig.axes[0].lines))  # 0 -> continuous path, legend warning
findings.expected: Either a small integer label set is grouped categorically, or the docstring states the numeric-dtype -> continuous rule and the legend warning suggests casting labels to str.
findings.actual: n_lines=0, n_coll=7 + UserWarning: legend is not supported for continuous or matrix-valued hue; ignoring legend. (str labels: n_lines=3, legend=['a','b','c'])

findings.title: Datasets with differing feature counts crash plot() with a raw numpy vstack error from the reduce stage, while hyp.align alone handles the same input
findings.description: hyp.plot([ (50,10) array, (50,7) array ], ...) -- with or without align= -- raises numpy's 'all the input array dimensions except for the concatenation axis must match exactly, but along dimension 1, the array at index 0 has size 10 and the array at index 1 has size 7' from reduce's np.vstack. No hypertools-level message tells the user the problem is unequal feature counts across datasets. Inconsistently, hyp.align([...], align='hyper') on the same input succeeds (pads internally), so the plot pipeline is stricter than its own alignment stage with no explanation.
findings.expected: Either the pipeline pads/handles mixed feature counts (as hyp.align does) or a clear ValueError: 'datasets have differing numbers of features (10 vs 7); hypertools requires equal feature counts for reduce -- pad or align first.'
findings.actual: ValueError: all the input array dimensions except for the concatenation axis must match exactly, but along dimension 1, the array at index 0 has size 10 and the array at index 1 has size 7

findings.title: One plot() call emits stage warnings twice: legacy reduce-dict DeprecationWarning x2 and hyperalign row-trim UserWarning x2
findings.description: Because plot() runs reduce twice (inside analyze(), then again to bring data to display dims) the legacy {'model','params'} reduce spec's DeprecationWarning fires 2x per call; the alignment 'alignment keeps only the 30 row(s) common to all datasets' UserWarning also fires 2x. Measured: DeprecationWarnings in one plot() call: 2; trim warnings in one plot() call: 2. Duplicate warnings train users to ignore them. (plot.py's own cluster spec handling explicitly dedupes its DeprecationWarning -- 'do NOT double-warn' comment, line ~1886 -- so the codebase already treats this as a bug class.)

print(sum(1 for i in w if i.category is DeprecationWarning))  # 2

findings.title: Silent dimensionality fallbacks are inconsistent: n_rows < ndims warns, but n_features < ndims (2-col data with ndims=3; ndims=20 on 10 features) is silent
findings.description: reduce() warns 'The number of rows in your data is less than ndims. The data will be reduced to the number of rows.' for short data, but when the FEATURE count is below ndims it silently returns the data unchanged: plot(2-col data, ndims=3) silently renders a 2-D square-frame plot; plot(10-col data, ndims=20, return_model=True) silently returns 10-D xform_data. Behavior is reasonable (dims cannot be invented) but the asymmetric signaling means an explicit ndims request can be quietly ignored.
findings.expected: A UserWarning mirroring the rows case, e.g. 'data has 2 features; cannot reduce to ndims=3 -- plotting in 2-D.'
findings.actual: xform_dim=(40, 2), 2-D axes, zero warnings (verified with warnings.simplefilter('always')); ndims=20 on 10-feature data likewise silent, xform_dim=(50, 10)

findings.title: plot(cluster=...) rejects sklearn-style instances that hyp.cluster itself accepts (and whose error message advertises)
findings.description: hyp.cluster(D, cluster=KMeans(n_clusters=3)) works (3 labels), and hyp.cluster's unknown-name error explicitly says '(or pass a scikit-learn style instance directly)'. plot(align=<Aligner instance>) also works. But plot(cluster=KMeans(n_clusters=3)) raises 'Invalid cluster model specified; should be string or dictionary!' because plot.py's cluster branch (lines 1870-1907) only handles str/dict. Inconsistent spec surface across stage kwargs of the same function and with the stage's own dispatcher.
findings.repro:
import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '/Users/jmanning/hypertools')
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
rng = np.random.default_rng(9)
D = np.vstack([rng.normal(i*6, 1, (30, 8)) for i in range(3)])
hyp.plot(D, fmt='.', cluster=KMeans(n_clusters=3), show=False)
findings.expected: Instance accepted (grouped traces), matching hyp.cluster and plot()'s own align=/reduce= handling.
findings.actual: ValueError: Invalid cluster model specified; should be string or dictionary!  (hyp.cluster with the same instance: OK, n_labels=3; plot align=HyperAlign() instance: OK)
